P1.evidence: No setter notes existed to read back — the prospect came off an Instagram ad and opened with 'I do know what I got into, but I don't know what this call is about', which the rep handled calmly. The frame was three-part, not four: 'I just want to understand what's going on, what have you tried, and where you're trying to get to in terms of fitness, health. And if there's alignment, we can talk about it, for sure. If not, that's fine, too.' Agreement asked and given ('Sounds good?'). Open question ran: 'walk me through, like, what's the main thing you're trying to fix now?'

P2.evidence: Height was asked ('And how tall are you'), weight and age were volunteered and only recapped ('Okay, so you're 34'). Occupation was never asked — the rep inferred it from 'You said you're working a lot' and later from the prospect calling himself a business guy. Nutrition was the one properly executed check and was run thoroughly: 'how about nutrition? How do you treat your body?', 'do you follow any diets?', then fish, eggs and dairy. Everything else was skipped. Most consequential: no health-condition question and no injury or movement-limitation question at all, on a 34-year-old who states 'I've never, ever done any exercise' and was about to be recommended loaded ballistic training. Sleep, energy and results from current training were never raised.

P3.evidence: Best-attempted phase. The bridge to deeper drive ran twice and hard: 'why is that so important to you?' then 'Just think about it for a second. What's the reason that you actually want to get in shape? Why?' The forward-projection ran: 'in three months, or let's say six months down the road... what opens up to you? Like this new way of life? Like what changes for you?' and when the prospect said it would not change his life the rep challenged it rather than accepting: 'Do you really believe that if you change your body, how you feel with your body, how you show up, and how you feel, that won't change your life?' The impact-on-others layer was supplied by the rep rather than elicited — he asked only 'How old are they?' and then delivered the daughters argument himself, so P3f and P3g are partial. No reflect-back landed because the prospect explicitly refused the frame: 'it's not something that's like a before and after in my life.' The surface goal questions on aesthetics, mobility/strength/energy and 'something you can't do' were never asked.

P4.evidence: The prospect volunteered all three past attempts unprompted before the rep asked anything, so P4a and P4b are misses — the script credits asking. The root-cause question did run: 'have you thought about deep down what's been behind that, that you didn't enjoy or wanted to actually make that change in the past?' The prospect named the gap himself and named it accurately — 'I don't like it enough. So not to make it into my schedule' and 'I'd rather watch a TV series than work out' — which is exactly what P4e asks for. The information-isn't-the-problem move surfaced late and only under pressure, at 00:36:26: 'the difference is in the accountability, especially.'

P5.evidence: Three of four moves absent — no 'what does life look like in two years if nothing changes', no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not'. The line in the sand ran almost verbatim, but late and as a rebuttal rather than as a frame: 'So this is the, like, the moment of drawing the line in the sand. And like... I'm doing something and not just talking about it.' The prospect had already supplied his own consequence — a father who is 75 and 'a crippled old guy' — and the rep used it in P3 rather than building the two-year cost of inaction on it.

P6.evidence: The belief check ran cleanly and in the right place, before delivery and price: 'If you had the right training, a simple nutrition, and someone like Trevor in your corner, all built around your life actually, would you agree that you would get to your goal?' — answered 'definitely'. The all-in check was never asked in that form before presenting; the equivalent, 'Is there anything else holding you back?', came after the number as an objection isolation. Note the prospect pre-empted the close with 'Sounds expensive. That's what I'm waiting to hear' at 00:30:33, and the rep pressed on to P6 anyway, which was the right call.

P11.evidence: Never reachable. The rep began to move there — 'next thing is we need to book you with Trevor' — but the prospect interrupted for the price, refused it outright, and the rep disqualified. No payment attempt, no onboarding booking, no agreement, no welcome sequence.

objection_plays.detail: Best OC execution in the batch. Isolation ran twice — 'finances aside, are you 100% sure that you can actually achieve your goals with Trevor?' and 'Is there anything else holding you back?' — and got a clean 'No'. The how-not-whether framing ran in peer register: 'We're business guys, we can work things out, yeah? So we don't have anything set in stone, like payment plans, but if there's a will, there's a way.' Permission was asked properly: 'So you're open for an open discussion about finances?' Of the six financial-picture questions, cash on hand ran ('what's your liquid cash right now on your hand?') and credit cards ran, plus an off-script credit-score question. Monthly surplus after bills, number of cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto/stocks/investments were all skipped — and the answer to the first question was zero, which the rep did not treat as the stopping point it was.

'for me to think about it and give you an answer? Or how does it go?' at 00:33:48. The first OA move ran in substance — 'are you 100% sure that you can actually achieve your goals with Trevor?' — and so did 'anything else holding you back'. The rest did not: no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no 'that man you want to be — how does HE decide right now?' Given the prospect had just described three abandoned attempts, that last move was the one the call was set up for and it never ran.

The known script gap, in its purest form. The prospect ran an explicit feature-by-feature comparison against free YouTube calisthenics he is currently doing and succeeding with, conceded every advantage of the paid offer including accountability, and still chose free: 'But one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest.' There is no scripted play for a cheaper alternative that is working. The rep improvised — conceded the content is all on YouTube, then narrowed to accountability and programming — and the prospect agreed with the reframe without moving. Objection C assumes capacity to pay is the blocker; here perceived incremental value was.

Second script gap — a request for a smaller first step. The prospect asked, in effect, for an entry-level product: buy the cheap used bicycle, find out whether you like cycling, then spend $6,000 a year later. There is no scripted response and no product to point at, so the rep agreed with the reasoning and disqualified.

notes: Discovery was thin where it mattered — no health or injury screen at all on someone who has never trained — but the deep-why work and the money play were the strongest in the batch, and the rep held his frame under an unusually articulate prospect who sells for a living. The real lesson is not about this rep: the call was lost to free content plus a missing entry-level rung, and the script has no move for either.
